title: Proposal to Add Text Messaging Service in National Anti-Violence Helpline to Facilitate Quick Reporting
what_it_is: Proposal to Add Text Messaging Service in National Anti-Violence Helpline to Facilitate Quick Reporting

sections.label: NAVH helpline consolidation and reporting
sections.summary: NAVH consolidates 10 helplines, received 8,400 calls from 18 January to end-December 2021, and MSF will add web or mobile reporting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: NAVH is a consolidation of 10 helplines into a single helpline to make it easier to report abuse and violence, reduce call waiting time and provide quicker support to callers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Since it started operations on 18 January 2021 until end-December 2021, NAVH has received 8,400 calls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In line with efforts to make it easier to report abuse and violence, MSF will enhance NAVH to allow multiple modes of reporting, such as via a web link or mobile application.

sections.label: NAVH enhancements and SMS 71999
sections.summary: Enhancements roll out by end-2022, MSF will study text messaging feasibility, and the public can use SMS 71999 for emergencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The enhancements will be rolled out by end-2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MSF will also study the feasibility and need for text messaging service to complement NAVH and web/mobile application in subsequent enhancements, taking into account considerations, such as the security of clients’ data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: If members of the public require emergency assistance but are unable to call 999, they should use the SMS 71999 service of the Singapore Police Force.

sections.label: Survivor or bystander reporting
sections.summary: The person could be the survivor or victim or a bystander, and the suggestion about other jurisdictions will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This person could either be the survivor/victim himself or herself, as well as a bystander.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will study the suggestion you have made about what the other jurisdictions are doing.

sections.label: Data security and staged rollout
sections.summary: Data security is of utmost importance, and implementation plans will be rolled out in stages to keep the system stable for callers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Indeed, the security of the data is of utmost importance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will be rolling out those implementation plans in stages to make sure that the system is stable, and also that when callers dial in, they get help.
